rounds.text: HEC Infra Projects Ltd trades at an attractive valuation of 12x P/E and 11.55x against a sector benchmark of 13.85x, while offering an EV/EBITDA of 8.15x that also undercuts its sector median of 9.66x [E1, E6, E11]. This modest multiple contrasts sharply with exceptional fundamental momentum, demonstrated by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 36% and an extraordinary 5-year compounded profit growth of 110% [E15, E19]. Profitability metrics are equally compelling, with ROE at 21.2% and ROCE at 21.4%, significantly outpacing their respective sector benchmarks of 14.61% and 17.27% [E9, E10, E13]. Operational efficiency has also structurally improved, as debtor days dropped from 94.9 to 55.4 days and overall working capital requirements compressed from 92.2 days to 40.4 days [E59, E60]. Furthermore, promoters have increased their skin in the game, lifting their shareholding to 74.93% by June 2026 from 73.20% in September 2023 [E40], supported by a high-confidence rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 [E62]. Conceded: the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% and has experienced deceleration in long-term sales alongside a low cash conversion of 0.23x against reported profits [E4, E14, E33].

Serious vulnerabilities lurk beneath the surface of HEC Infra Projects Ltd, starting with severe cash conversion weakness where operating cash flow sits at just 0.23x of reported profit for March 2026, meaning profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation [E33]. This is compounded by rising debt, with total borrowings increasing to Rs 44 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 38 Cr a year prior [E38], alongside a stagnant long-term sales growth profile showing a meager 4% compounded rate over ten years [E14]. Institutional backing has completely evaporated, with domestic institutions slashing their stake from 8.52% in September 2023 down to absolute zero by June 2026 [E41]. Shareholders also face a complete lack of capital return through dividends [E4] despite reported profits, and screen checks explicitly flag that earnings growth is decelerating [E67]. Furthermore, the equity carries substantial historical volatility of 61.9% [E52] and a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.9% [E51], leaving investors exposed to poor one-year price performance of -10.9% to -14% [E24, E50]. Conceded: [E19].

While the bear highlights a low cash conversion ratio for March 2026 [E33], this figure ignores that absolute operating and free cash flows each stood at a positive Rs 3 Cr [E34, E35], alongside dramatic improvements in debtor days from 94.9 to 55.4 [E59] and working capital requirements dropping from 92.2 to 40.4 days [E60]. Conceded: [E38]. While long-term ten-year sales growth is modest [E14], it obscures explosive medium-term expansion, including a 36% five-year and 51% three-year compounded sales growth [E15, E16]. Although domestic institutional holdings fell [E41], promoters increased their skin in the game to 74.93% [E40], demonstrating strong insider alignment. Conceded: [E4]. Furthermore, the technical and fundamental outlook is powerfully supported by a price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E48], sector-beating returns on capital and equity [E8, E9], and an overall rules-based screen score of 83 out of 100 pointing to high-confidence buy territory [E62].

Conceded: [E34, E35]. While absolute operating and free cash flows stand at Rs 3 Cr, the operating cash flow is only 30 percent of operating profit, producing a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.23x that explicitly signals profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection and warrant checking for receivables or accruals [E33, E36]. Although the bull champions explosive medium-term sales expansion [E15, E16], this must be weighed against a pedestrian 10-year compounded sales growth rate of just 4 percent [E14] and an explicit screen warning that earnings growth is decelerating [E67]. Conceded: [E40]. The increase in promoter stake occurs alongside domestic institutional holding plummeting completely from 8.52 percent down to 0.00 percent [E41], reflecting a total desertion by professional institutional oversight. Finally, while the bull highlights moving averages and screen scores [E48, E62], these technical indicators completely ignore severe underlying structural vulnerabilities including a negative 14 percent one-year share price growth [E24], a harsh historical peak-to-trough drawdown of 51.9 percent [E51], and an exceptionally high annualised volatility of 61.9 percent [E52].
